content: NHS Wales is the official corporate entity responsible for the National Health Service in Wales. Historically, it was part of the same National Health Service as England, but it is now a devolved system. NHS Wales, known in Welsh as GIG Cymru, is managed and operated by the Health and Social Care Department of the Welsh Assembly Government. The majority of the population in Wales has access to a District General Hospital. These hospitals provide a variety of medical services, including outpatient care, inpatient care, and day case procedures. Some of these hospitals also offer specialized services, such as burns and plastic surgery or cardiac surgery. In addition to hospital-based care, NHS Wales delivers a range of community services. These include district nursing, health visiting, midwifery, and community-based therapies such as speech therapy, physiotherapy, and occupational therapy. Local Health Boards (LHBs) were established in 2003 to replace the previous Health Authorities in Wales. A typical Welsh NHS Trust oversees all hospitals within a specific region, as well as community care and mental health services. There are 12 regional Trusts that manage groups of local authority areas. Additionally, there is a dedicated Trust for the Welsh Ambulance Service and another, Velindre, which operates nationwide agencies and services. Wales has one primary teaching hospital, the University Hospital of Wales, which is located in Cardiff. Another key organization within the NHS Wales structure is Health Commission Wales. This executive agency of the Welsh Assembly Government is tasked with centrally organizing and funding all tertiary care and other highly specialized services. It also provides advice and guidance on specialist services to other parts of NHS Wales. NHS Direct is available in Wales, offering callers the option to communicate in either Welsh or English.
